Hey Voat, can multinational corporations like GE and Coca-Cola be sustainability leaders?

I work for with one of these businesses and believe me, they don't give a rat's ass about sustainability. We routinely throw away huge numbers of wooden pallets, for example. and there are literally no recycling bins anywhere in the building as far as I know. they preach greenness and sell it to their customers, but do not practice it on-plant at all.

I know first hand that some companies do aggressively prioritize recycling and lots of other actions that benefit the common good (energy efficiency, treating workers well, etc.). Often times these are really successful companies too.

Of course there are others, which I think are unfortunately still way too common, that don't do anything without an immediate and obvious self interest, and worse still the few who work against sustainability.

I wouldn't say this business works against it, but they certainly aren't about to go out of their way. There's no profit in it. People routinely have to throw away plastics and stuff like that just because there's no bins anywhere on plant but the professional building.

I once worked as an associate for a retail chain store- I once got letter encouraging me to 'Be green, Save the trees; get direct deposit!' and later that same day dumping hundreds of cardboard boxes into the dumpster out back because getting a recycling company to come pick it up was more expensive. Absolutely disgusting.

Reading the article, I learned that a survey of experts from the World Wildlife Foundation, Greenpeace, United Nations, Oxfam and Carbon Disclosure Project ranked Unilever way above the other 4 companies who were recognized as the top 5 (Patagonia, Interface, Marks & Spencer, Natura, and Ikea).

This is the top 5 corporate sustainability leaders, so while it doesn't speak to the value of big corporate power, it does rank some of the best within that given group.
